segments: And one day, when the Arabs attacked the baggage train of the Franks,
the King of England became enraged,
and he pursued the Arabs with mighty force.
And the Arabs were scattered, and most of them fled;
there remained with Saladin only seventeen men from among the chosen of the Arabs,
together with the horn-blowers and the standard-bearers.
And had not the Franks feared lest there might be an ambush and held back,
otherwise, on that very day they would have captured Saladin,
and the cause of the Arabs would have fallen.
And in those days Saladin sent architects and some horsemen,
that they might go and empty the fortress of Baghras of provisions and dismantle it.
And when they went and dismantled a little of it,
they heard that Leo, the ruler of Cilicia, was preparing to attack them,
and they abandoned it and fled.
And the Antiochenes heard of their flight,
and they came to Baghras,
and found in it twelve thousand measures of wheat.
And they brought them to Antioch,
and it was a great relief to them,
because famine had grown severe there at that time.
And after some days Leo came and prevailed over the Franks,
and took Baghras from them.
And Saladin sent and dismantled Ashkelon and emptied it of people,
because the Franks had already rebuilt Jaffa and settled in it,
and it lies between Jerusalem and Ashkelon.
For this reason the Arabs said,
"We are not able to guard it."
And Saladin went to Jerusalem,
and inspected it and fortified it with men and so forth.
And in those days Mu'izz al-Din, the lord of Melitene, came to him,
complaining against his father, Sultan Qilij Arslan, and against his brothers,
that they wished to take Melitene away from him.
And Saladin received him with honor,
and gave him the daughter of his brother al-Malik al-'Adil as a wife,
and sent him back to Melitene,
and encouraged him no longer to fear his brothers or his father.
And the King of England sent an envoy to Saladin and said to him:
"Behold, the men of our side and of your side have been consumed by the sword,
and until when shall it be like this? For our swords and your swords are drunk with blood.
Restore now the lands that you took from us,
especially Jerusalem, our house of worship,
for the sake of which we set out,
so that we may leave and depart."
